source.label: 193 company-tagged problems plus 2 reconstructed drills
source.note: Practice snapshot from a third-party company-tag dataset: 193 tagged problems plus 2 reconstructed drills, grouped by pattern. Scores rank this dataset, not the probability of your next question. The 30-day and 6-month badges describe source windows at import, not live recency; the original import date was not recorded. Solution buttons include Python reference code and built-in tests; other rows link to LeetCode. Prioritize pattern coverage and spoken reasoning over finishing the entire list.

script.say: Before I code, let me confirm the input sizes, value ranges, edge cases like empty input, and what to return when there is no answer.
The straightforward way is ... which is O(...). That works, but it is too slow at n = ...
This looks like a ... problem because ... . If I ... , I can get to O(...). Does that sound good before I write it?
Narrate intent, not syntax: here I keep the window valid, here I record the answer. Name helpers for each step.
Walk the example by hand, then an edge case: empty, one element, all equal, the no-answer case.
Time is O(...) because ... ; space is O(...) for ... . If I had more time I would ...

patterns.name: Heaps and scheduling
patterns.template:
import heapq

heap = []
heapq.heappush(heap, (priority, tiebreak, item))  # tiebreak avoids comparing items
while heap:
    priority, _, item = heapq.heappop(heap)
    # process, push follow-ups

# max-heap: push -value
# top k largest: keep a min-heap of size k
pitfalls: Python heapq is a min-heap; negate for max.
Tuples compare element by element; add a counter tiebreak before objects.
Event simulation: pop every event at the same timestamp before starting new work.

patterns.name: BFS and graphs
pitfalls: Mark visited when you enqueue, not when you pop, or nodes get queued twice.
Level-by-level: loop range(len(queue)) to count minutes or layers.
Weighted edges need Dijkstra, not BFS.
Cycle detection in topological sort: processed count < n.

patterns.name: Sliding window and two pointers
signals: longest or shortest subarray or substring
at most k distinct or k changes
patterns.template:
left = 0
for right, x in enumerate(items):
    add(x)
    while window_invalid():
        remove(items[left])
        left += 1
    best = max(best, right - left + 1)
pitfalls: Shrinking only works when validity is monotonic (adding never fixes, removing never breaks).
Counting subarrays: add right - left + 1 per step.
Negative numbers break product and sum windows; reach for prefix sums.

patterns.name: Intervals
pitfalls: Ask whether touching endpoints overlap.
Sort by end for greedy keep-the-most problems, by start for merging.
Rooms: heap of end times, or sweep over sorted starts and ends.

patterns.name: Hashing and prefix sums
patterns.template:
from collections import defaultdict

seen = defaultdict(int)
seen[0] = 1  # empty prefix
prefix = count = 0
for x in nums:
    prefix += x
    count += seen[prefix - k]
    seen[prefix] += 1
pitfalls: Seed the empty prefix (seen[0] = 1).
Count before you insert the current prefix.
Tuple keys for signatures; lists are not hashable.

patterns.name: Binary search on the answer
signals: minimize the maximum or maximize the minimum
smallest speed, capacity, or size that works
a feasibility check that is monotonic
pitfalls: Say why feasible() is monotonic before coding.
Pick bounds that are definitely valid and invalid (max element, total sum).
lo < hi with hi = mid never loops forever; lo <= hi variants do if you forget +1.

patterns.name: DP basics
signals: choices at each step with overlapping subproblems
two strings compared character by character
patterns.template:
# 1. state: what does dp[i] mean in words
# 2. transition: dp[i] from smaller states
# 3. base case, then iterate in dependency order
dp = [base] + [INF] * n
for i in range(1, n + 1):
    for choice in choices(i):
        dp[i] = min(dp[i], dp[i - cost(choice)] + 1)
pitfalls: Say the state in one sentence before writing code.
Roll arrays to O(n) space only after it works.
Greedy needs a proof or a brute-force check; say which.

patterns.name: Union-find
pitfalls: Track component count as you union.
Per-component data lives at the root.
Union-find does not support deletes; process offline or rebuild.

patterns.name: Design data structures
patterns.template:
from collections import OrderedDict

items = OrderedDict()
items.move_to_end(key)          # mark recent
items.popitem(last=False)       # evict oldest
pitfalls: Interviewers may ban OrderedDict; know the hash map plus doubly linked list version.
Updating an existing key also refreshes recency.
Capacity 0 edge case.

patterns.name: Stacks and greedy
signals: best choice with a counting argument
pitfalls: Write down which pairs interact before coding the loop.
Store counts on the stack for run-length removals.
Greedy: argue why the local choice is safe.

patterns.name: Trees
pitfalls: Decide what each call returns before coding.
Path problems often return one value and track another globally.
Level order needs BFS with range(len(queue)).

patterns.name: Linked lists
patterns.template:
prev, cur = None, head  # full-list reversal
while cur:
    nxt = cur.next
    cur.next = prev  # save next before rewiring
    prev, cur = cur, nxt
head = prev
pitfalls: A dummy head removes edge cases at the front.
Save next before rewiring.
Fast and slow pointers for middles and cycles.

patterns.name: Backtracking
signals: search a board for a word
pitfalls: Copy the path when saving it.
Prune early; it is the whole performance story.
Undo every change on the way back.

patterns.name: Math and bits
signals: powers of two or binary digits
patterns.template:
x & 1        # lowest bit
x >> 1       # divide by 2
x & (x - 1)  # drop lowest set bit
bin(x).count('1')
pitfalls: Check overflow assumptions out loud even in Python.
Try small cases by hand to find the formula.
Negative numbers and bit shifts differ by language.

patterns.name: Arrays, strings, simulation
signals: do exactly what the rules say
build a string step by step
pitfalls: Restate the rules with an example first.
Off-by-one at both ends.
Build strings with a list, then join.

problems.title: Task scheduling with a memory limit, at most 2 of a type in parallel
problems.insight: Simulate time with a min-heap of running tasks' end times; at each event, start every waiting task that fits.
approach: Clarify first: are tasks taken strictly in order, or can a later task jump a blocked one? Can tasks start at the same instant others finish? Is the goal the finish time or a feasibility check?
Reject any task whose memory alone exceeds the limit.
Keep used memory and a per-type running count.
At time now, scan waiting tasks in index order and start each one that fits both limits.
Advance now to the earliest end time, free every task ending then, and repeat.
problems.time: O(n^2 + n log n) with the simple waiting scan
edge_cases: Task larger than the memory limit
problems.prompt: Each task has a type, a memory need, and a duration. The machine has a memory limit and may run at most 2 tasks of the same type at once. Tasks are prioritized by index; whenever capacity frees up, start every waiting task that fits, earliest index first. Return when all tasks finish, or -1 if some task can never run. (Reconstructed practice variant; the original candidate report is not linked in this snapshot. Confirm the exact scheduling rules before solving. This simulation follows index priority and does not prove an optimal makespan.)

problems.title: Grid BFS where you can jump 1 to K cells
problems.insight: BFS still gives shortest moves; prune each slide when you hit a cell reached earlier, because that cell covers everything beyond it.
approach: Clarify: can you jump over walls? (Assume no.) Are diagonal moves allowed? Is K the same for every cell?
BFS from start with dist grid.
From each cell, slide up to K steps in each direction.
Stop the slide at a wall, the edge, or a cell with a smaller distance; skip but continue past cells at the same distance.
Return dist at the target or -1.
problems.time: O(rows * cols * K) worst-case upper bound; pruning reduces repeated scans in practice
problems.prompt: Given a grid of open cells '.' and walls '#', a start, an end, and K, each move goes 1 to K cells in one of four directions without passing through a wall. Return the minimum number of moves, or -1. (Reconstructed practice variant matching the Codeforces 877D movement rules. The original candidate report is not linked in this snapshot; practice the pattern without assuming it will appear.)

problems.title: Minimum Operations to Reduce an Integer to 0
problems.insight: Read bits from the right: a lone 1 costs one subtract, a run of 1s costs one add that carries it away.
approach: If the low two bits are 11, add 1.
Else if the low bit is 1, subtract 1.
Else shift right for free.

problems.title: String Compression
problems.insight: Read pointer scans each run; write pointer writes char plus count in place.
approach: read walks to the end of the current run.
Write the char, then the count digits if run length > 1.
Return write.
edge_cases: Run length 10 or more writes multiple digits

problems.title: Time Needed to Rearrange a Binary String
problems.insight: Each 1 needs as many seconds as zeros before it, but it can be stuck one second behind the 1 ahead of it.
approach: Count zeros seen.
For each 1 after a zero: seconds = max(seconds + 1, zeros).

problems.title: LFU Cache
problems.insight: Bucket keys by frequency, each bucket in LRU order, and track the minimum frequency for O(1) eviction.
approach: values, freq maps; buckets: freq to OrderedDict.
Touch: move key from bucket f to f + 1, bump min_freq if bucket f emptied.
Evict: pop the oldest key in the min_freq bucket.
New key resets min_freq to 1.
edge_cases: Put on an existing key counts as a use

problems.title: Closest Equal Element Queries
problems.insight: Group indices by value; the nearest equal element is a neighbor in that sorted list, wrapping around the circle.
approach: Map value to sorted indices.
For each index, check the previous and next index in its list (wrapping).
Distance is min(gap, n - gap); -1 if the value appears once.
edge_cases: Two copies: both neighbors are the same index

problems.title: Smallest Substring With Identical Characters I
problems.insight: Binary search the longest allowed run L; a run of length r needs r // (L + 1) flips, except L = 1 which must alternate.
approach: Search L from 1 to n.
L = 1: mismatches against 0101 and 1010, take the min.
L > 1: sum run // (L + 1) over runs.
Smallest L with flips <= numOps.

problems.title: Smallest Substring With Identical Characters II
Maximum Product of Three Numbers
problems.insight: The answer is either the three largest or the largest times the two most negative.
approach: nlargest(3) and nsmallest(2).
Return the max of the two products.

problems.title: Subarray Product Less Than K
problems.insight: Positive numbers make the product monotonic, so a shrinking window counts all valid subarrays ending at right.
approach: Multiply in nums[right].
While product >= k, divide out nums[left].
Add right - left + 1.

problems.title: Minimize Malware Spread
problems.insight: Removing an initial node only saves its component if it is that component's only infected node.
approach: Union-find over the adjacency matrix.
Component sizes and infected counts.
Pick the node in a single-infection component with the largest size, smallest index on ties; else the smallest initial.

problems.title: Maximum Number of Occurrences of a Substring
Maximum Palindromes After Operations
problems.insight: Swaps are free across words, so only total letter pairs matter; fill the shortest words first.
approach: Count pairs across all letters.
Sort word lengths.
Each word needs length // 2 pairs; take while pairs last.
edge_cases: Odd lengths take any letter as center

problems.title: Merge Intervals
problems.insight: Sort by start; each interval either extends the last merged one or starts a new one.
approach: Sort.
If start <= last end, extend last end.
Else append.

problems.title: LRU Cache
problems.insight: Hash map for O(1) lookup plus an order structure for O(1) recency updates and eviction.
approach: OrderedDict: move_to_end on get and put.
Pop the oldest when over capacity.
Be ready to write the doubly linked list version.

problems.title: Course Schedule II
problems.insight: Kahn's algorithm: repeatedly take courses with no remaining prerequisites.
approach: Build adjacency from prerequisite to course and count indegrees.
Queue all indegree-zero courses.
Pop, append to order, decrement neighbors, enqueue new zeros.
If order is shorter than n, there is a cycle.

problems.title: Power Grid Maintenance
problems.insight: Grids never change, so union-find once and keep a min-heap per grid with lazy deletion of offline stations.
approach: Union all connections.
Heap of station ids per root.
Query: if online return x, else pop offline tops and return the min or -1.
edge_cases: Station offline but grid has others

problems.title: Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters
problems.insight: Track each char's last index; on a repeat inside the window, jump left past it.
approach: Map char to last index.
If last index >= left, move left to last index + 1.
Update best each step.

problems.title: Minimize Maximum Component Cost
problems.insight: Kruskal: add the cheapest edges until there are at most k components; the last edge added is the answer.
approach: Sort edges by weight.
Union until components <= k.
Return the weight of the last successful union (0 if n <= k).

problems.title: Group Anagrams
problems.insight: Anagrams share a letter-count signature; use it as the dict key.
approach: Signature: tuple of 26 counts (or sorted string).
Append each word to its group.

problems.title: Split a String in Balanced Strings
Minimum Time to Visit All Houses
Number of Islands
problems.insight: Each unvisited land cell starts a new island; flood fill marks the rest of it.
approach: Scan cells.
On a '1', count an island and BFS to sink connected land.
Mark visited when enqueuing.

problems.title: Count the Number of Fair Pairs
problems.insight: Pairs in [lower, upper] = pairs <= upper minus pairs <= lower - 1, each counted with two pointers on the sorted array.
approach: Sort (pair counts ignore order).
Count pairs with sum <= limit using two pointers.
Subtract the two counts.

problems.title: Maximum Frequency Stack
problems.insight: Keep a stack per frequency level; a value appears in every level up to its count, so pop from the top level.
approach: freq counter and stacks by level.
push: increment, append to that level.
pop: from max level, drop the level when empty.

problems.title: Delete and Earn
problems.insight: Taking value v forbids v - 1 and v + 1: house robber over sorted distinct values.
approach: points[v] = v * count.
Track take and skip; adjacent values cannot both be taken.
edge_cases: Gaps between values reset the constraint

problems.title: Decrypt String from Alphabet to Integer Mapping
Check Whether Two Strings are Almost Equivalent
Check If a Number Is Majority Element in a Sorted Array
Maximum Number That Makes Result of Bitwise AND Zero
Find Subarray With Bitwise OR Closest to K
Equalize Strings by Adding or Removing Characters at Ends
Find the Minimum Area to Cover All Ones II
Find the Minimum Area to Cover All Ones I
Find the Last Marked Nodes in Tree
Longest Common Subsequence
problems.insight: dp[i][j] = LCS of prefixes; match extends the diagonal, else take the better skip.
approach: Iterate characters of both strings.
Keep one rolling row.

problems.title: Minimum Removals to Balance Array
problems.insight: After sorting, keep the longest window where max <= k * min; remove the rest.
approach: Sort.
Two pointers: advance left while nums[right] > k * nums[left].
Answer is n minus the longest window.

problems.title: Asteroid Collision
problems.insight: Only a right-mover on the stack meeting a left-mover collides; resolve against the stack top until one survives.
approach: For each asteroid, while it moves left and the top moves right, compare sizes.
Pop smaller tops, cancel equal ones, stop when the new one dies.
edge_cases: Left-movers at the start never collide

problems.title: K-diff Pairs in an Array
problems.insight: Count unique pairs by their smaller value; k = 0 needs a duplicate instead.
approach: Counter of nums.
k = 0: values with count > 1.
Else: values v with v + k present.

problems.title: All Nodes Distance K in Binary Tree
Count Subarrays With Median K
problems.insight: Map each value to +1 or -1 relative to k; a subarray containing k has median k when its balance is 0 or 1.
approach: Find k's index; every valid subarray includes it under the distinct-value constraint.
Count balances of all left extensions.
For each right extension, add matches for balance 0 and 1.
edge_cases: Even-length subarrays use the left middle

problems.title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock
Merge k Sorted Lists
problems.insight: The next output node is the smallest current head across all lists.
approach: Push each list head with an index tiebreak.
Pop the smallest, append it, push its next node.
Stop when the heap is empty.

problems.title: Minimum Window Substring
problems.insight: Expand until every needed char is covered, then shrink while surplus chars sit at the left.
approach: Counter of t; missing = len(t).
Expand right, decrementing need and missing.
When missing hits 0, shrink surplus, record the window, release the leftmost needed char.

problems.title: Kth Largest Element in an Array
problems.insight: A min-heap of size k keeps the k largest; its top is the answer.
approach: Push each number.
Pop when the heap grows past k.
Return the top. Mention quickselect for average O(n).

problems.title: Top K Frequent Elements
problems.insight: Frequencies are bounded by n, so bucket by frequency instead of sorting.
approach: Count with Counter.
Place each value in bucket[freq].
Walk buckets from high to low until k values collected.
edge_cases: k equals number of distinct values

problems.title: Minimum Number of Taps to Open to Water a Garden
problems.insight: Turn taps into intervals, then it is jump game II: from each left edge, how far right can you reach.
approach: reach[left] = max right for taps starting there.
Greedy sweep: when x passes the covered boundary, open a tap and extend to the best reach seen.
If x passes every reachable point, return -1.

problems.title: Koko Eating Bananas
problems.insight: Hours needed falls as speed rises, so binary search the smallest feasible speed.
approach: lo = 1, hi = max pile.
Feasible if sum of ceil(pile / speed) <= h.

problems.title: Optimal Account Balancing
problems.insight: Reduce to net balances, then backtrack: settle the first nonzero balance into each opposite-sign account.
approach: Net balance per person, drop zeros.
DFS: skip settled, try each opposite sign, dedupe equal amounts.
Exact cancel short-circuits.
problems.time: O(n!) worst case, where n is the number of nonzero balances; clarify the participant bound

problems.title: Remove All Adjacent Duplicates in String II
problems.insight: Stack of (char, run length); pop when a run hits k, which lets neighbors merge.
approach: Increment the top run or push a new one.
Pop at k.
Rebuild the string.

problems.title: Maximum Team Size with Overlapping Intervals
Meeting Rooms II
problems.insight: Rooms needed = max overlapping meetings; a heap of end times reuses the room that frees first.
approach: Sort by start.
If the earliest end <= start, reuse that room.
Else open a new room. Answer is the heap size.

problems.title: Coin Change
problems.insight: dp[x] = fewest coins for amount x; try each coin as the last one.
approach: dp[0] = 0, others infinity.
dp[x] = min(dp[x - c] + 1).
Return -1 if unreachable.

problems.title: Rotting Oranges
problems.insight: Multi-source BFS from every rotten orange at once; levels are minutes.
approach: Queue all rotten cells, count fresh ones.
Process one level per minute, rotting fresh neighbors.
Return minutes, or -1 if fresh remain.

problems.title: Word Ladder
problems.insight: BFS over words; wildcard patterns like h*t find neighbors without comparing every pair.
approach: Return 0 if endWord is missing.
Bucket words by each wildcard pattern.
BFS from beginWord, popping buckets so each is used once.

problems.title: Largest Number After Digit Swaps by Parity
Verify Preorder Sequence in Binary Search Tree
Longest Increasing Subsequence
problems.insight: Patience sorting: keep the smallest possible tail for each length and binary search where each number goes.
approach: For each number, bisect_left in tails.
Append or replace.

problems.title: Number of Visible People in a Queue
Minimum Difficulty of a Job Schedule
Network Delay Time
problems.insight: Weighted shortest paths from one source: Dijkstra, then take the max.
approach: Adjacency list.
Heap of (time, node); finalize a node on first pop.
Answer is the max distance if all nodes reached, else -1.

problems.title: Count Vowel Substrings of a String
Minimum Replacements to Sort the Array
Find Median from Data Stream
problems.insight: Two heaps split the stream into a lower and upper half; the median sits at their tops.
approach: Max-heap for the lower half, min-heap for the upper.
Push through the lower heap into the upper to keep order.
Rebalance so lower has equal or one more element.

problems.title: Top K Frequent Words
problems.insight: Sort key (-count, word) gives frequency first, then alphabetical; nsmallest takes the top k.
approach: Counter.
heapq.nsmallest(k, words, key=(-count, word)).

problems.title: Longest Increasing Path in a Matrix
Reorganize String
problems.insight: Greedily place the most frequent remaining char, holding the last one out for a turn.
approach: Max-heap of (count, char).
Pop the top, append it, push back the previously held char.
If a char is still held at the end, it is impossible.
problems.time: O(n log a), a = alphabet size
edge_cases: One char more than half the length

problems.title: Longest Continuous Subarray With Absolute Diff Less Than or Equal to Limit
Using a Robot to Print the Lexicographically Smallest String
Vertical Order Traversal of a Binary Tree
Remove Stones to Minimize the Total
problems.insight: Always halve the current largest pile; a max-heap gives it in O(log n).
approach: Negate piles into a min-heap.
k times: pop the largest, push it back after removing floor(x/2).
Return the sum.

problems.title: Minimum Edge Reversals So Every Node Is Reachable
Maximum Number of Ways to Partition an Array
Maximum Number of Non-overlapping Palindrome Substrings
Shortest Distance to Target String in a Circular Array
Least Number of Unique Integers after K Removals
Max Chunks To Make Sorted II
Finding the Number of Visible Mountains
Number of Operations to Make Network Connected
problems.insight: You need n - 1 cables total; with enough, the answer is components - 1.
approach: If cables < n - 1, return -1.
Union-find to count components.

problems.title: Lexicographically Minimum String After Removing Stars
Shortest Bridge
problems.insight: Mark one island fully, then BFS outward from all its cells; the first ring touching the other island is the answer.
approach: Find any land cell, DFS to mark the first island and collect its cells.
Multi-source BFS through water, one ring per flip.
Return flips when a ring reaches unmarked land.

problems.title: Longest Substring Of All Vowels in Order
Construct Binary Tree from Preorder and Inorder Traversal
Time Taken to Cross the Door
Partition Array Into Two Arrays to Minimize Sum Difference
Subarray Sum Equals K
problems.insight: A subarray sums to k when two prefix sums differ by k; count earlier prefixes equal to prefix - k.
approach: seen[0] = 1.
For each prefix, add seen[prefix - k], then record prefix.

problems.title: Angle Between Hands of a Clock
Fruit Into Baskets
problems.insight: Longest window with at most 2 distinct values.
approach: Count fruit types in the window.
Shrink while more than 2 types.
Track the max length.

problems.title: Construct Binary Search Tree from Preorder Traversal
Amount of Time for Binary Tree to Be Infected
Find the Smallest Divisor Given a Threshold
Convert Sorted List to Binary Search Tree
Longest Consecutive Sequence
problems.insight: Only start counting at numbers with no predecessor, so each run is walked once.
approach: Put numbers in a set.
For v with v-1 absent, count upward.
Track the best.

problems.title: Minimum Equal Sum of Two Arrays After Replacing Zeros
